subject: FinLytics onboarding — model shortlist & workload sizing
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finlytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: model shortlist + token/context questions for onboarding

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited to get started. Before our internal kickoff tomorrow, the product team asked for a short write-up on model recommendations and a rough sizing estimate so they can validate infra and procurement. High-level ask below:

- Primary use cases: document Q&A (ingested legal and financial docs), single-turn assistant for SMEs, and a short-form summarization endpoint used in-line in the product UI.
- Expected active users at launch: 2,000 (ramp to 5k over 3 months).
- Avg docs per user: 4, average doc length ~1,500 tokens. Typical retrieval pipeline will pass a 2–3 chunk context (we're still tuning chunk size).
- SLA: sub-600ms median retrieval+inference for single-turn assistant; summaries can be >1s.
- Compliance: data stays in US region.

Can you share: model shortlist (recommendations + tradeoffs), context length requirements you expect, and a ballpark monthly token estimate (best/worst case)? I've attached sample prompts and a small usage CSV to help.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Product, FinLytics
[sent attachment: FinLytics_MVP_prompt_samples.pdf, FinLytics_usage_sample.csv]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist + token/context questions for onboarding

Hi Sarah — great to meet you yesterday. Attaching our onboarding checklist and a short initial sizing. Brief summary here, we can iterate after we see full prompt set and request logs.

Model shortlist (initial recommendations):
- Llama3-Chat-13B (fp16/qat) — best mix of quality and cost for chat + Q&A; good at instruction following and fewer hallucinations than older Llama variants.
- Mistral-Instruct-8B (int8) — strong for summarization and shorter completions, lower cost; may need prompting tweaks on domain-specific legal language.
- MPT-30B-Chat (8k context, quantized) — candidate if you want more reasoning/headroom for longer summaries; higher cost and memory footprint.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized) — fallback for high-quality, longer-context tasks if throughput allows.

Context length guidance:
- Retrieval chunks: 1,000–2,000 tokens is typical; for legal passages we recommend 2,000 tokens chunk to preserve paragraph context.
- For single-turn assistant and Q&A, 4k context should cover combined prompt + relevant retrieved snippets for most flows. Consider 8k for long-document summarization endpoints.

Ballpark token estimates (monthly) — two scenarios based on your CSV sample and stated active users:
- Conservative (launch): 2,000 active users, 3 requests/user/day, avg request payload+reply = 1,200 tokens => 2k * 3 * 30 * 1,200 = ~216M tokens/month.
- Mid ramp (3 months): 4,000 active users, 4 requests/user/day, avg 1,400 tokens => 4k * 4 * 30 * 1,400 = ~672M tokens/month.
- Peak (worst): 5,000 users, 5 requests/day, avg 1,600 tokens => 5k * 5 * 30 * 1,600 = ~1.2B tokens/month.

Operational suggestions:
- Start on hosted Redwood API with model routing: default to Llama3-Chat-13B, fallback to Mistral-Instruct-8B for short summaries to save cost.
- Enable prefix/KV caching on high-frequency prompts (e.g., standard templates) — often reduces token spend by ~10–30% for repetitive queries.
- For predictable throughput consider Redwood Dedicated pool at 1–2 GPU-equivalents if 600ms median is required at launch — we'll refine after load testing.

I've attached: redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf (walkthrough), and added the CSV to our drive link. Can we sync tomorrow after your internal kickoff?

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[sent attachment: redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FinLytics sizing proposal (notes + math)

Team — quick internal note before tomorrow's sync with FinLytics. I pulled numbers from Sarah's sample and our conservative assumptions. Please review and flag if you see problems.

Assumptions (from attachment + convo):
- Launch active users: 2,000; target peak: 5,000 (3-month ramp).
- Requests per user: 3/day (launch), 5/day (peak).
- Average prompt tokens: 500 (includes retrieved chunks); avg completion tokens: 700; total per request = 1,200 tokens (adjustable).

Monthly token math examples: (30 days)
- Launch: 2k * 3 * 30 * 1,200 = 216,000,000 tokens (~216M)
- Ramp: 4k * 4 * 30 * 1,400 = 672,000,000 tokens (~672M)
- Peak: 5k * 5 * 30 * 1,600 = 1,200,000,000 tokens (~1.2B)

Throughput sizing thoughts:
- If we serve Llama3-Chat-13B on fp16, approximate single-GPU sustained throughput (generation limited) ~12–18 tokens/sec depending on sequence length and batching. For 600ms median latency we'll need conservative batching and autoscale.
- For Mistral-Instruct-8B in int8, throughput ~25–40 tokens/sec on same hardware — good for short summaries and bursty traffic.
- Recommendation: start hosted with autoscale; run a 48–72 hour load test using synthetic traffic modeled from their CSV. If 600ms median is non-negotiable at launch, plan for Dedicated capacity equivalent to 2 high-end GPUs for steady traffic + autoscale headroom.

Action items:
1) Diego — prepare a load test plan and synthetic traffic generator (T+1).
2) Monica — confirm whether FinLytics requires private VPC or can stay hosted in US region. Also confirm encryption/KMS needs.
3) Stephanie — draft an initial rollout plan and fallback routing policy (Llama3 -> Mistral fallback).

If all agree I'll send the summary back to Sarah and propose an initial load test window next week.

Thanks,
Markus

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: FinLytics sizing proposal (notes + math)

Agree with the approach. A couple of tweaks:
- Increase recommended context for summarization endpoint to 8k (they explicitly mentioned long legal docs).
- For the dedicated sizing toggle consider a mixed pool: 1x high-memory GPU for Falcon-40B fallbacks (if needed) + 2x standard GPUs for Llama3/Mistral. That gives a safety net without full 40B cost for steady state.
- I'll reach out to Sarah after you propose load test windows to confirm data residency and KMS.

Monica

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: FinLytics: next steps & proposed load test window

Hi Sarah — quick summary from our side and proposed next steps. See below and let us know if this matches your internal planning.

Summary recommendations:
- Model shortlist: primary = Llama3-Chat-13B, cost-saver = Mistral-Instruct-8B, long-context candidate = MPT-30B-Chat or Falcon-40B fallback.
- Context: 2k chunks for retrieval; 4k default context for chat/Q&A; 8k for long-document summarization.
- Token estimate (launch): ~216M tokens/month; mid-ramp ~672M; peak ~1.2B.
- We'll enable prefix/KV caching and suggest starting on hosted API with model routing; move to Dedicated if load tests show median-inference >600ms consistently.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) FinLytics to confirm whether hosted US-region is OK and share any additional sample prompts or higher-volume logs.
2) Redwood to run synthetic load test (48 hours). Proposed window: Wed 07/07 02:00 - Thu 07/08 02:00 UTC. Diego will share test plan.
3) Post-test: review p95/p99 latencies, cost projection, and recommend Dedicated sizing if needed.

Attachments: I included our onboarding checklist and noted their sample CSV on the shared drive.

Would you like us to schedule the load test window now or wait until your legal team confirms data handling?

Best,
Markus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
